title: Quick start your first sound without hardware

blocks.text: You can use the dashboard before connecting either the robot or Hydrasynth. The browser can make sound from simulated signals or the three bundled movement recordings. The six saved voice demonstrations also play without an API key. New music and rap generation need a configured ElevenLabs account and internet access; the first sound exercise below uses neither.

The five-minute walkthrough begins after installation. A first installation can take longer because it downloads Python packages and a local speech model. The Ubuntu/Debian installer does not connect motors, send physical MIDI commands or record an audio input during setup.
Install once on Ubuntu or Debian

Open a terminal. Install Git if it is missing, then clone the published repository. If it is private, use the GitHub authentication provided by the repository owner. The owner must commit and push the installer and application changes before a new laptop can receive them through Git.

sudo apt-get install git
git clone https://github.com/richardsavery/hydrasynth.git
cd hydrasynth
bash tools/setup.sh

Run the setup command as your ordinary desktop user. It asks for your sudo password only if system packages are missing. At the hidden API key prompt, paste this laptop’s key or press Enter to skip. No characters are displayed while pasting. Once setup finishes, start the application:
make dashboard-sonify
Hear something and try a signal

items: Leave the terminal open. In the same laptop’s browser, open http://127.0.0.1:8790/#synth-mixer.
Open Setup → Connections. Set Synth output to Browser audio and press Test sound. Check the computer’s output device and volume if you hear nothing.
Open Use → Synth mixer. In Signal mixes, set Signals from to Simulated demo signals. This supplies a changing input without a recording, live stream or robot.

Choose Movement as Input 1 in Mix A. In the Filter cutoff card, set Signal mix to Mix A. Press Play in Shape your sound: the cutoff should now follow the simulated movement. Try the sound and tempo controls, then press Stop. A parameter left on Manual will not follow a signal.
To try recorded movement, select a bundled recording in Connections and return to the mixer with Signals from set to Connections input. Keep the input source and your mappings consistent.
For a no-cost voice preview, open Use → Rap response, expand Voice demos and play a saved demonstration. Listening does not choose a new voice or generate a rap.

blocks.text: Tabs are workspaces within one application. Navigating between them can leave playback and robot control running; use the appropriate Stop control when you want to end an activity. Loading or viewing a page does not start robot movement.
Stop and return later

Stop playback in the dashboard. If you are collecting study data, wait for the researcher Study panel to report Saved locally before ending the server. In the terminal running the dashboard, press Ctrl+C and let shutdown finish. To return later, open a terminal in the hydrasynth folder, run make dashboard-sonify and open the same address. Installation does not create a login service or background launcher.

The application records study events automatically unless explicitly disabled for a development run. Read the study chapter before involving participants. The ordinary participant interface hides the researcher controls; it does not disable recording.

title: Installation and launch reference

blocks.text: What you need

The automated installer targets Ubuntu/Debian Linux. It requires Python 3.10 or newer, a normal user account and internet access for missing packages and the initial model download. Allow several GB of free space for the environment, download caches, recordings and generated audio. Speakers or headphones are enough for browser playback; a microphone is needed only when you choose to record. Node.js is optional for running the application and is needed for the JavaScript test suite.

rows: build-essential, pkg-config, libasound2-dev
Build the native C tools against Linux ALSA.
alsa-utils
Device diagnostics, including aconnect and arecord.
python3-venv and .venv
Create an isolated Python environment for this checkout.
requirements-robot.txt
Install serial and Dynamixel support for the robot.
requirements-rap-response.txt
Install local transcription and vocal processing dependencies.
requirements-beat-tracking.txt
Install local beat analysis for Music mixer and Keirzo timing.
FFmpeg and ffprobe
Prepare, inspect and validate audio files.
Whisper Small in var/whisper/small
Transcribe microphone recordings locally after initial download.
Node.js
Run JavaScript regression tests; not required to serve the dashboard.

blocks.text: Setup reuses an existing usable .venv, installs the two requirements files, builds hydractl and hydra-audio, runs their self-tests, prepares the model and checks that it loads on this CPU. Existing credentials and local data are retained. Setup does not make a paid provider request, so successful installation alone does not prove that the ElevenLabs account can access every generation feature.
Installer options

bash tools/setup.sh --skip-model --no-key
bash tools/setup.sh --skip-system
PYTHON=/path/to/python3 bash tools/setup.sh
bash tools/setup.sh --help

Use --skip-model for a quicker preview installation that does not yet need microphone transcription. Typed rap input remains available, but generation still requires a provider key. Use --no-key to leave credential provisioning until later. Use --skip-system only when an administrator has already installed the required packages, or you have provided equivalent build/audio dependencies. It skips apt and sudo, not the dependency checks, Python installation or build.

The installer uses /usr/bin/python3 by default when creating a new environment, avoiding an unconfigured asdf shim. PYTHON selects an alternative for a new environment; an existing .venv retains its original interpreter. A broken or too-old environment is left intact with an explanatory error. Move it aside and recreate it with a suitable interpreter rather than copying an environment from another computer. The repository’s .tool-versions selects Python 3.12.9 and Node.js 22.20.0 for asdf users.
Equivalent manual installation

sudo apt-get install build-essential pkg-config libasound2-dev \
  alsa-utils python3-venv ffmpeg ca-certificates
/usr/bin/python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-robot.txt -r requirements-rap-response.txt -r requirements-beat-tracking.txt
make all
.venv/bin/python tools/prepare_rap_transcription.py
.venv/bin/python tools/configure_api_key.py

On another Linux distribution, install its equivalent packages and use --skip-system. A matching ALSA development package can also be extracted into var/native-deps on a machine without installation privileges; docs/linux.md describes this fallback. Normal package installation is the simpler arrangement for a fleet of laptops.
Choose the launch mode

rows: make dashboard-sonify
Everyday browser work with no native Hydrasynth required. It starts the server in demo mode.
make dashboard
The connected native Hydrasynth service, incoming telemetry and local command broker. Requires the intended MIDI device.
make dashboard-sonify DASHBOARD_ARGS='--port 8791'
A different local port. Open that port in the browser; browser storage is separate for each origin.
make dashboard-sonify DASHBOARD_ARGS='--study-dir /path/to/local/study-data'
An explicit study storage location. Use the same path consistently.
make dashboard-sonify RECORDINGS_DIR=/path/to/recordings
Use another recordings library instead of the bundled default.

blocks.text: The direct equivalent of the normal no-hardware launch is .venv/bin/python tools/hydra_dashboard.py --demo. Extra server options can be appended there or supplied through DASHBOARD_ARGS. Keep the default loopback host, 127.0.0.1, for normal operation. Each laptop runs its own server; opening its address on another laptop will address that other laptop instead. The local audio and study APIs enforce local access, so changing the bind address is not a turnkey shared server deployment.
macOS and other platforms

On a Mac, finish Apple’s Command Line Tools installation if needed, then run bash tools/setup.sh in the clone. The Mac installer prepares Homebrew, FFmpeg, Python dependencies, native CoreMIDI/Core Audio tools and Whisper Small. It preserves existing keys, model files and local data. Use the same setup command after git pull for updates, then make dashboard-sonify to start. See docs/macos.md for the complete Mac procedure and permissions. Native Windows requires a separate port and is not supported.

title: Provisioning six laptops and API credentials

blocks.text: Prepare a reproducible set of machines

items: Publish the application version you intend to use: commit and push the required repository changes before cloning the other laptops. Record the chosen Git revision for the session.
Label the physical laptops, for example laptop-01 through laptop-06. Clone the same repository revision on each and run setup as the user who will operate the application.
Provision that laptop’s credentials separately from Git. Let its first dashboard run create its own study database and installation ID.
Use the same browser and address convention on each laptop. Test browser sound, the bundled recordings and voice demos; then grant microphone or Web MIDI permission only for the features you need.
Record each physical label alongside the installation ID displayed in the researcher Study panel. Synchronize laptop clocks before data collection.
If hardware will be used, complete the physical connection and calibration checks on the actual rig before participant use.

blocks.text: Recommended credential arrangement

For laptops you manage under trusted organiser accounts, provision one restricted ElevenLabs key per laptop, named hydrasynth-laptop-01 through hydrasynth-laptop-06. Separate keys let you replace or revoke one machine’s credential independently. The provider supports endpoint restrictions and per-key credit limits; usage still counts against the workspace quota. Service account keys are intended for backend workloads when available in your workspace. Check the current account controls at https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/administration/workspaces/api-keys.

Distribute credentials privately through a password manager or a USB drive you control, then enter the appropriate key in the hidden installer prompt. The application’s Python backend uses the key; it is not intended to be pasted into dashboard fields, browser JavaScript, source code or a shared chat. A person who controls the laptop account can nevertheless read its local files. Owner-only permissions protect against other ordinary accounts, not against the machine’s owner or administrator.

For somebody else’s own computer, use their own authorised provider credential, or arrange a central authenticated generation service if they must not possess your provider secret. This repository currently makes provider calls from each local Python backend and does not implement that central service. A single shared key can work technically, but it removes independent revocation and gives every recipient the same credential.
Set replace or transfer a key

.venv/bin/python tools/configure_api_key.py
.venv/bin/python tools/configure_api_key.py --replace

The first command keeps an existing saved key; --replace prompts for a replacement. Paste the key alone, without quotation marks, spaces or line breaks. Press Enter to skip without changing the existing file. In a noninteractive terminal, configuration is skipped instead of echoing a secret. The helper writes the project’s .env atomically with mode 600, meaning owner read/write only, and preserves other settings. .env is Git-ignored; .env.example is a blank template, not a place to put a real key.

To provision a prepared private file, use the following pattern from the checkout, substituting the actual USB path. This replaces .env, so use the prompt instead when other existing settings must be preserved.
install -m 600 /media/USB/laptop-01.env .env

A private provisioning file contains the setting ELEVENLABS_API_KEY followed by an equals sign and that machine’s key. Restart a running dashboard after changing it. An ELEVENLABS_API_KEY already set in the process environment takes precedence over .env; update or unset it if a newly saved key appears to have no effect. Never put a real key in Git, even in a private repository. Replace a disclosed key through the provider and update the affected laptop.
What consumes credits

New music generation and new raps use the provider. The rap pipeline can include lyric planning, music generation, stem separation and voice conversion. Grant the endpoint access needed by the features you plan to use and confirm account access before a session. Local transcription, local pitch/autotune edits, browser synthesis, saved voice demos and playback of already saved audio do not need new provider requests. Canceling an in-flight generation cannot guarantee that no credits were consumed. In Music mixer, set Next track to Loop before playing a saved track if you want to avoid automatic replacement generation.
Save time on the speech model

Download Whisper Small on one machine, then copy only the complete var/whisper/small directory to the same relative location in the other clones before running setup. The model used here is approximately 464 MiB. Setup recognises complete model files and checks that they load locally. A copied model avoids repeated downloads but does not replace installation of the Python transcription dependencies.

# On each new clone, using the actual USB path:
mkdir -p var/whisper
cp -a /media/USB/small var/whisper/
bash tools/setup.sh

Create .venv and build native binaries separately on every laptop. Do not clone another machine’s complete var directory or study database: that can duplicate its installation identity, recordings and private data. Transfer head-calibration.json only for the same physical robot and review the calibration before powered operation. Copying the model, provisioning the key and transferring robot calibration are three separate tasks.

title: Connections choose input and sound output

blocks.text: Connections is the starting point for choosing movement data and the destination for Synth mixer sound. Open Setup → Connections, or http://127.0.0.1:8790/#connections. Input data and sound output are separate choices: a recording can drive a real Hydrasynth, and live movement can drive browser audio. You do not need an API key, robot or synth to use the bundled recordings, browser synth or voice demos.

blocks.caption: Connections separates the data source on the left from sound output on the right. The browser-only path works with the robot and synth disconnected.

blocks.text: Start with a bundled recording

items: In Input, choose Recording. Wait for the list to load. A normal clone includes three compressed recordings; the dashboard reads these directly, so do not unzip them.
Select a recording. Check its title and the input summary near the top of the dashboard. If you added files while the server was running, use Refresh recordings beside Choose a recording.
In Output, leave Synth output set to Browser audio. Press Test sound and listen through the computer’s selected speakers or headphones. The status should report that the test sound played.
Open Use → Synth mixer. Choose Connections input under Signals from when you want the selected recording to drive mappings. Select a field in a Signal mix, map it to a parameter, then press Play.
Return to Connections whenever you need another recording or output. Merely opening this workspace does not stop a mixer that is playing. Use the mixer’s Stop control when you want to stop.

blocks.text: Recordings contain numerical data, not prerecorded music. Selecting one does not play a soundtrack. Music mixer uses the same data as a control source but needs an existing or newly generated track for its sound.
Check browser sound before investigating MIDI

Test sound uses the browser’s current audio destination. Select the desired device in Linux sound settings and check application and device volumes. Its status confirms scheduled playback, not audible speaker output. Check whether the browser tab is muted if the test is silent.

Music mixer and Rap response play through browser audio. Changing Synth output to MIDI device changes the Synth route; it does not send generated music to the synth. The Hydrasynth needs its own audible output path, such as headphones or an audio connection to an interface. MIDI carries performance commands, not the synth’s recorded audio.
Use a live movement stream

items: Start the movement-data sender on the robot or replay computer. Obtain its WebSocket address. For a sender running on this same laptop, the standard address is ws://localhost:8765.
In Connections, select Live stream. Enter Stream address and press Connect live. Allow browser local-network access if prompted for a network sender.

Wait for usable fields to appear in the live monitor. A connected socket or a greeting alone is not movement data. Check the message rate, freshness and a changing numeric signal before opening a mixer.
Choose a channel and signal in the monitor to inspect its graph. Position and velocity are separate inputs. For arrays or tensors, the monitor shows a reduced value and a bounded preview.

In either mixer, set Signals from to Connections input and choose the discovered fields. Start playback explicitly. Keep Reconnect automatically selected if you want the browser to reconnect after a socket interruption.
Use Disconnect to end the live connection. Use Return to recording, then choose the required recording, when returning to recorded data.

blocks.text: Pause display freezes the inspection display only. The browser still receives movement, learns ranges and drives active mappings. Reset learned ranges changes calibration, not the sender. Use it after a change in movement range, not as a substitute for reconnecting a broken stream. A channel becomes stale when it has not supplied usable data for more than three seconds; updates on other channels do not make its old values current.

The skeleton channel supports ZED BODY_18 data as 54 flat values or 18 nested XYZ triples. With Connections input selected, the mixers default to seven body-region movement controls: whole body, head, torso, each arm and each leg. Each joint’s movement speed combines changes along X, Y and Z in metres per second; a region averages its tracked joints’ speeds. Skeleton detail also offers 18 individual joint movement signals and the original 54 XYZ position axes plus raw arrays. Existing selected fields stay visible when changing the detail view, and saved mappings retain their meaning. Motion uses consecutive valid frames and resets after tracking loss, timestamp resets or gaps over half a second. Recorded movement needs t_recv or stamp timestamps and is calculated before downsampling. Original positions remain in metres, with X forward, Y left and Z up in the camera reference frame.

A live socket closure stops Synth playback. Automatic reconnect does not restart a performance; press Play again after the stream returns. An open connection with a temporarily stale required channel waits for fresh values. A connected light does not mean every mapped input is valid.

rows: Cannot connect
Confirm the sender is running, its host and port match, and the laptop can reach it. A generic WebSocket error does not distinguish a network, permission, TLS or sender problem.
Connected, no usable data
Start replay or the robot data feed. Status greetings contain no values. Open Troubleshooting for invalid-message reasons and a valid JSON example.
One source is unavailable
Check that the expected channel is still sending and that the saved field belongs to this recording or stream. Choose the intended replacement explicitly.
Graph seems frozen
Check Pause display and the freshness indicator. Resuming display does not restart a stopped transport.

blocks.text: Connect the Hydrasynth through the browser

items: Power and connect the Hydrasynth. In Connections, choose MIDI device under Synth output, then press Connect MIDI device if permission or device access needs retrying.
Allow browser MIDI access. Check MIDI destination and select the intended instrument if more than one device matches. Do not select an unrelated MIDI output just to remove an error.
Use PARAM RX mode = NRPN · full engine for the full parameter catalog, and set PARAM RX on the Hydrasynth to NRPN. Choose CC · compatibility only when both sides are set for CC.
Leave Updates / second at 50 initially; the available choices are 25, 50 and 100. Enable PGM CHG RX on the synth only when you want the dashboard to select stored patches.
Open Synth mixer and press Play. The dashboard sends on MIDI channel 1. Connecting alone does not start playback or change patches.
If notes continue after stopping, use Connections → Stop all MIDI notes. After a device disconnect, confirm the destination and press Play again.

blocks.text: The browser tries the saved destination or a single identifiable Hydrasynth automatically. A changed port ID can be matched by unique name and manufacturer; multiple matches require selection. Native ALSA and browser Web MIDI are separate routes, so a successful native device list does not grant browser permission.

title: Signal mixes turn data into reusable musical controls

blocks.text: Synth mixer and Music mixer share the same Signal mixes workflow. A signal mix is a named control value built from one or more numerical inputs. It does not mix sound. Each input is reduced to one number, normalized to a 0–100% range, and combined with the others. You then connect that result to synth parameters or music-channel effects. Begin with one input and one destination so that you can hear what each choice does.

blocks.caption: Signal mixes before an input is selected. Choose an input, inspect its range and then assign the mix to a parameter; the empty history here is expected while stopped.

blocks.text: Build and inspect a mix

items: Set Signals from. Connections input uses the recording or live stream chosen in Connections. Simulated demo signals supplies Movement, Energy and Pace for learning the controls without a sender.
In a Signal mix card, edit its name to describe the intended behavior, for example Arm energy or Slow brightness. Names help you identify the same control when assigning it to several destinations.
Choose an input. The menu groups available signals by source channel and distinguishes joint position from velocity. Check the raw numerical readout, normalized meter and recent-history graph.
Expand Auto learn or Fixed range beneath the input. Choose Read as if the field supports several reductions. Leave a scalar joint on its normal direct reading; select an array reduction deliberately.

Press + Input to add another source to this mix, then choose Combine inputs. A mix supports up to six inputs. Press + Signal mix to make another independent control; either mixer supports up to four mixes.
Assign the mix to a parameter or channel effect. A mix with no destination can be inspected without changing the sound.

blocks.text: Changing Signals from replaces the mixes’ input selections with fields appropriate to the new mode and detaches shared links. Save a session before switching modes if you want to preserve a carefully prepared mapping.

rows: Direct value
Use one scalar reading, such as a labelled joint position or velocity.
Average
Use the mean of an array. Positive and negative entries can cancel each other.
RMS magnitude
Use the size of an array’s values without positive and negative cancellation; useful when magnitude is more meaningful than direction.
Lowest value / Highest value
Follow the most extreme valid value in the selected array.
One element
Read one flattened array element. Element index starts at 0: index 0 is the first element. Keep the sender’s array layout consistent.

blocks.text: Calibrate input ranges

Auto learn expands the observed minimum and maximum as usable values arrive. For recordings, available saved bounds help establish the range; for live input, the app learns from fresh frames. A constant learned signal maps to the midpoint rather than causing a division error. Early values may therefore have a large effect until the performer has explored a representative range. Let the input cover its normal movement before deciding whether the output sweep is suitable.

items: Leave Range on Auto learn while observing a representative movement or recording segment.
Inspect the displayed bounds and normalized meter. Confirm that quiet and active movement occupy different parts of the range.
Press Freeze range to retain the learned bounds as a fixed calibration. This helps repeat a mapping consistently during a session.

For known units, choose Range = Fixed and enter Minimum and Maximum yourself. Use a finite minimum smaller than the maximum. Values beyond the bounds clamp at the corresponding end of the normalized range.
Press Learn again when the input scale changes and you want to replace the calibration. This is specific to the chosen input; it is not a reset of every mix.

blocks.text: Combine several inputs

rows: Average
Equal influence from each normalized input. A useful starting choice for several joints.
Weighted blend
A weighted average. Expand each input to set its Weight. For example, weights 3 and 1 give the first input three times the influence of the second.
Difference
Compares the first input against the average of the remaining inputs. Equal normalized values produce the midpoint; a larger first input moves upward and a smaller first input moves downward.
Lowest
Follows the smallest normalized input, so all inputs need to rise for the result to become high.
Highest
Follows the largest normalized input, so one active input can produce a high result.

blocks.text: Inputs are normalized before combination, so fields with very different raw scales can contribute together. A required missing input makes the mix unavailable. Remove unintended sources or choose replacements explicitly; the other inputs do not hide their absence.
Share definitions between the two mixers

items: On a prepared mix, press Share mix. It is now a shared definition in this browser.
Open the other mixer. Use the same Signals from mode, choose the definition under Shared signal mixes, then press Add shared mix.
Assign local destinations in the second mixer. The shared definition supplies the inputs and combination, while each mixer keeps its own synth parameters or stem-effect mappings.
When you switch between mixers, edits to shared input definitions, combination and fixed bounds are synchronized. Automatically learned ranges stay local.
Press Make independent if you want to branch the mix without subsequent shared edits. The current definition becomes an independent local copy.

blocks.text: Control the amount of influence

Signal strength controls each mapping’s influence. At 0%, the manual/base setting applies and the mapping does not wait for input. At 100%, the full mapped range applies. Intermediate values blend toward the base. Try 25–50% for a dramatic effect, then adjust From and To. Music frequency controls use logarithmic blending.

title: Synth mixer play and shape browser or Hydrasynth sound

blocks.text: Synth mixer has three areas: Shape your sound, Signal mixes, and Synth parameters. It creates notes and parameter changes locally. Browser output needs no provider key or generated track. MIDI output uses the destination selected in Connections. The small output label beside Shape your sound identifies the current route, so check it before troubleshooting silence.

blocks.caption: Synth mixer places the sound and transport controls above the named input mixes. Browser voices work without connected hardware.

blocks.text: First sound without hardware

items: In Connections, select Browser audio and confirm Test sound works. Open Use → Synth mixer.
Choose Browser voice = Pluck or Warm pad. Set Tempo · BPM to 96, Root to C and Scale to Minor pentatonic. Set Chord voices to 1 for a simple line or 3 for chords.
Leave Automatic sound changes at Off · keep current sound. This keeps the timbre stable while you learn the mapping controls.

Press Play. Existing manual parameters can produce sound without an active movement mapping. If a saved mapping is waiting for input, choose its correct source, set its Signal strength to 0%, or temporarily disable that parameter.
Choose Simulated demo signals under Signals from. Name a mix Movement brightness and select Movement. In the Filter cutoff card, choose that mix under Signal mix.
Listen while reducing Signal strength or changing the mapped range. Press Stop when finished. Save a named session if you want to preserve this experiment.

blocks.text: Browser voice offers Glass, Pluck, Warm pad, Reed, Bell, Soft bass and Custom. These browser recipes are separate from Hydrasynth factory patches. Tempo accepts 20–240 BPM and Chord voices accepts 1–8. Root and Scale constrain the musical pitches.
Use the parameter desk

blocks.caption: Parameter cards show the effective value, a manual base, the selected signal mix, Signal strength, and the expandable mapping range.

items: Find the desired existing card, or press + Parameter. Search in Find a parameter or narrow Group, then select the destination to add it.
Choose Manual in Signal mix to set the value directly. For an enum control, use its named choices; for a continuous control, use its slider.
Select a named mix to map the parameter. The manual slider becomes Base value, used at 0% Signal strength and as the reference for partial strength.
Open Range & response. Set From and To to the desired musical bounds. Start with a modest range, then widen it while listening.
Choose Response and optionally Reverse. Check the large effective-value readout and meter while the source moves.
Use Enabled/Disabled to retain a card but stop that parameter from contributing. Use the × button only when you want to remove the card.

blocks.text: The desk contains note, harmony, rhythm, timbre and effect destinations as well as the published Hydrasynth catalog. Hardware controls carry MIDI labeling. A MIDI only or unavailable reason means the current output cannot send that control; it is not evidence of a broken input. Hardware mappings remain saved when you switch to browser audio. Full-engine NRPN entries need NRPN selected in Connections. Reference catalog entries can include documented ambiguities; the interface does not invent a sendable address for unsupported definitions.

rows: Linear
Even progress from From to To as the normalized signal rises.
Smooth
Gentler movement near each end of the range.
Exponential
Less movement at the lower end, increasingly strong movement as the signal rises.
Inverse
Reverses the normalized signal. Reverse also changes direction, so avoid applying both unless that is intentional.
Steps
Quantizes the normalized signal into five levels. Useful for distinct changes rather than a continuous sweep.
Threshold
Switches between the two ends at the midpoint. Useful for an on/off-style musical change.

blocks.text: Build rhythm deliberately

Use + Parameter for Hits per 16 steps, Pattern rotation · steps, Note repeats · per step, Swing · %, Accent strength · %, Gate length · %, Note chance · %, or Tempo · BPM. The clock generates a repeating step pattern from the data; it does not detect a prerecorded beat inside a movement file. Fewer hits and lower note chance create more space. More repeats subdivide selected hits. Gate changes how long a note is held, while velocity changes its attack level.

For a clear demonstration, map one movement mix to Filter cutoff first. Then add Hits per 16 steps with From = 4 and To = 12. Keep pitch and tempo manual while listening to these two changes. If both mappings feel too active, lower each Signal strength separately. Reusing one mix creates a relationship between brightness and density, but their ranges and amounts remain independent.
Choose Hydrasynth patches

items: Connect MIDI and match PARAM RX as described in Connections. On the instrument, enable PGM CHG RX if patch selection is required.
Expand Sounds & patches. Choose Bank A–H and Patch 1–128, then press Select patch. These are the front-panel bank and one-based patch locations.
Listen to the selected patch before mapping many parameters. Patch selection replaces unsaved edits in the synth’s current edit buffer.
For changing sounds during playback, choose Cycle, Random or Follow mapping under Automatic sound changes. Choose Change every from 16, 32, 64 or 128 steps.
For a limited MIDI palette, choose Custom selection under Patch palette and enter locations such as A001, B017, H128. Verify each location contains an appropriate sound on this instrument.
For Follow mapping, add Sound palette position · % and map it to a mix. Return Automatic sound changes to Off when you need a stable patch.

blocks.text: Browser automatic sound changes select browser voices; MIDI changes select stored patches. Playback can continue after a brief patch transition. Parameter edits affect the current synth buffer rather than storing a patch permanently.
Understand stopped and waiting states

Switching dashboard workspaces keeps the Synth transport and parameter processing running. Stop is the explicit end of playback. Missing data in an enabled, available mapping above 0% strength makes the synth wait rather than substituting another source. Check which card is mapped, whether its mix has valid inputs and whether the output is MIDI or Browser audio. If a saved hardware mapping is unavailable in browser mode, it stays saved without pretending to affect the browser sound.

Previous version opens the older Synth mapping-tab interface and its independent settings. Loading sessions or changing connections can stop playback; verify the restored output and source before restarting.

title: Music mixer create instrumental tracks and shape their stems

blocks.text: Music mixer plays generated audio through the browser. A track is the musical recording; stems are separated instrument layers that can be adjusted independently. The workspace filters vocal stems out of its instrumental playback and mappings. A fresh Git clone provides movement recordings and voice demos, but does not automatically include music you generated on another laptop. New music and stem separation require an API key, internet access and provider credits; adjusting or replaying already prepared local audio does not generate a new performance by itself.

blocks.caption: Music mixer combines creation controls, reusable signal mixes and a desk for the master and instrumental stems. Saved tracks depend on audio retained on the local server.

blocks.text: Play existing music without automatic generation

items: Open Use → Music mixer. Set Next track to Loop before starting if you want only the current track to repeat.
Expand Recent tracks and choose a completed saved track. Press Refresh if a newly completed track is missing from the list.
Press Play saved track. Check the selected title and Playing status. The current track repeats in Loop mode without requesting a replacement.
Adjust the Master level, then the available stems. Scroll the mixing desk horizontally if some channels are outside the visible area.
Press Stop when done. Merely switching to another workspace leaves this transport running.

blocks.text: If no track is available, open a Sessions ZIP containing the intended music or generate a new track. ZIP exports include the selected generated audio and completed stems; older Sessions JSON files contain references only. Current Music mixer playback requires prepared instrumental stems. For an older track with missing stems, restore its complete session archive, use the Previous version interface’s preparation workflow, which uses credits, or choose a fully prepared track.
Generate a first instrumental track

items: Confirm the backend has its API key and FFmpeg setup. Address any setup message before generating.
In Create instrumental music, enter Next track prompt. A useful example is: Gentle instrumental electronic groove, spacious chords, clear bass and restrained percussion.
Set BPM, Key, Instruments and Track length. The length choices are 20, 40 or 60 seconds. For example, try 96 BPM, C minor, and synthesizer, bass, drums. Keep these fields consistent with the prompt.

Choose Next track deliberately. Loop creates a starting track if none is selected and then repeats it. Generate new and Generate similar enable continuing replacement generation after the starting track.

Press Start music, or Create starting track when that is the displayed action. Wait through music generation and stem preparation. The controls report the current stage rather than immediately presenting unfinished audio.
When playback begins, listen before adding mappings. Use Stop to end playback and prevent future automatic requests. Work already submitted can still finish and use credits.

blocks.text: Generated BPM, key and style are musical requests, not guaranteed measurements. Beats can drift and stems can contain bleed. Listen before synchronizing a robot or rap vocal.

rows: Loop
Repeats the current track. No replacement generation is requested.
Generate similar
Prepares another track from the prompt and, when available, a low-strength reference to the current audio.
Generate new
Prepares a fresh interpretation of the prompt. This is the default continuing-generation choice.
Choose old
Select Saved track for the next transition. The chosen old track then repeats until you choose another. This choice does not request new music or stem separation.

blocks.text: Generate new and Generate similar keep one spare track ready, including stems. When a transition consumes that spare, another can be requested; there is no session generation cap in this mixer. Editing the prompt, BPM, key, instruments or length while continuing generation is enabled updates the waiting request after a short typing pause. Keep an eye on Next track if several laptops share one provider account.

Up next describes pending music. Ready replacements crossfade near the loop boundary. If preparation is late, the current track repeats. If generation fails, it also keeps repeating until Retry next track succeeds. A temporary rejection because another music or stem job is active can retry after a delay, while failed or uncertain provider outcomes are not automatically resubmitted. Switching to Loop or Choose old stops further generation requests; already submitted work can finish and appear in Recent tracks. A crossfade already in progress completes before the following choice applies.
Mix manually first

rows: Volume fader
Sets the channel’s manual level. Master controls the combined output.
Mute
Silences a channel regardless of its mapped volume. Press again to restore it.
Solo
Available on stems. Isolates selected stems for listening and takes priority over mappings.
Pan
Places a channel between left and right.
Low pass / High pass
Reduce high or low frequencies respectively. Excessive filtering can make an otherwise playing channel nearly inaudible.
Delay / Reverb
Add repeats or a reverberant tail. These can remain audible briefly after a musical event.
Pitch shift
Shifts pitch from −12 to +12 semitones without changing duration. Master and stem shifts add together.
Playback speed
Master only, under More effects. Changes speed from 75% to 125% while preserving pitch and keeping the stems together.

blocks.text: Vertical meters show effective volume settings, not measured loudness. A high meter does not prove that the file is sounding. Local pitch/speed processing adds a short delay, and large pitch shifts can alter transients.
Add movement-driven effects

items: Under Signal mixes, choose Connections input or Simulated demo signals. Prepare a named mix using the input and calibration workflow described earlier.
On the intended channel, press + Map a signal. Choose Signal mix, then the effect under Controls.
Open Range & direction. For a first pan experiment, choose a moderate span such as From = −0.5 and To = 0.5. Use Reverse if movement should travel the other way.
Adjust Signal strength while listening. At 0%, the channel keeps its manual setting. At 100%, it follows the full mapped range.
Reuse the same mix on another channel or another effect. For example, let movement pan a percussion stem while gently opening the master low-pass filter.
Check mute, solo and manual levels when a volume mapping seems ineffective. Mapped volume multiplies the fader, so a fader at zero remains silent.

blocks.text: An audible channel waits for the valid inputs needed by its active mappings. Missing inputs on muted or solo-excluded stems do not silence the other audible stems. If the transport says Waiting for mapped input, inspect the relevant mix, its fields, and the source mode; reduce that route to 0% or remove it when comparing with manual playback. Preferences survive Stop and reload, but reloading does not start audio or arm new generation.

title: Rap response record type perform and reuse replies

blocks.text: Rap response turns a short message into a rhyming answer, or performs words you supply. It supports a generated full mix and an isolated voice over a playing mixer. Open Use → Rap response. The six fixed voice choices are Eva, Cold Android, Peter, Elowen, Maisie and Warren. A voice identity is consistent, while delivery and expression can vary between generated performances.

blocks.caption: Rap response keeps message creation on the left and the transcript, lyrics and playback on the right. Voice demos at the bottom can be auditioned without generation.

blocks.text: Audition voices without using credits

items: Expand Voice demos at the bottom of the workspace.
Press Play Eva, Play Cold Android or another named button. Only one demo plays at a time.
Use its Stop button, choose a different demo, or close Voice demos to end the preview.
Select the identity you want under Voice for new raps. Listening to a demo does not change that selection automatically.

blocks.text: The demos are bundled and need no key. They use clean audio, without your Pitch shift or Autotune settings. New delivery and timing can differ.
Create a typed reply

items: Set What should the rap say? to Reply to me.
Type a concise message in Or type something. For example: I finally finished my project and want to celebrate with a calm victory song.
Choose Voice for new raps, Beat style and Length. Beat style offers Boom bap, Trap and Lo-fi; Length offers 4 or 8 bars.
Choose New response. Use With generated beat · full mix for a standalone result, or Over main music · isolated voice when you already have a backing mixer playing.
Set Requested BPM between 70 and 140. If a valid backing is playing in isolated-voice mode, its tempo is used for the new rap and must be within that range.
Choose whether to enable Play when my new response is ready. Press Make rap response once and follow the status through writing, performing, separating, converting and local effects.
When Rap ready appears, inspect You said and The rap, choose the desired Play this response mode, and press its playback button if it did not auto-play.

blocks.text: Record a message

items: Choose Reply to me and set the desired voice, style, length and output mode before starting. These settings are captured for the request.
Use headphones if music is already playing. This reduces backing audio entering the microphone.
Press Record a message and grant browser microphone access. Speak a clear, short message. The maximum recording is 30 seconds.
Press Finish & rap when finished. At the limit, recording finishes automatically. This begins transcription and the rap workflow; it is not merely a recording preview button.
Watch the status and resulting transcript. Use Cancel if you need to abandon the remaining work. Leaving Rap response also releases the microphone and stops this workspace’s playback.
If the transcript is unsuitable, use typed input for a new request with the intended message. A previously submitted generation is separate and may still have used credits.

blocks.text: Microphone transcription runs locally with Whisper Small after its model has been installed. The original microphone recording is not sent to ElevenLabs. The transcript or supplied lyrics are sent for the requested provider workflow, and generated vocal audio is sent for voice conversion. New raps use provider services and credits even though transcription itself is local. The study recorder retains microphone attempts, including canceled attempts, when study recording is enabled; canceling generation is not a request to delete study data. The generated full mix is also sent to the provider for stem separation.

If local transcription is unavailable, the record control explains the missing setup and typed input remains available when the generation service is configured. If microphone access is unavailable or denied, check the browser’s site permission and Linux input-device selection. Check the displayed backend setup issues separately: giving microphone permission does not configure an API key.
Perform your own lyrics

items: Set What should the rap say? to Rap my words. The recording row is hidden and the text field becomes Words to rap.
Enter the words exactly as you want them supplied to the performance. Preserve line breaks for your intended lyrical grouping.
Keep within 48 words for 4 bars or 96 words for 8 bars. The on-screen counter shows your current allowance.
Set the voice, effects, beat and playback choices, then press Rap my words. This skips writing a reply and submits your text as the lyrics.

blocks.text: Play over a mixer or with the generated beat

For Over main music, first start Music mixer or Synth mixer, then navigate to Rap response. Navigation keeps the backing running. The isolated vocal is scheduled at the next bar and uses the backing’s audio clock. If the backing is stopped, invalid or changing speed, wait for a stable transport and press Play again. A generated performance can drift from the backing even though its start is aligned. Changing or stopping the backing stops the vocal so that it does not continue against an unrelated clock.

With generated beat plays the processed voice and its own generated instrumental. Full-mix microphone recording and completed full-mix playback stop other dashboard audio; submitting a typed generation alone does not. Play this response controls how a completed result is heard; New response controls the next request. Use Rap volume for listening balance, Stop voice or Stop mix to stop the result, and Download full mix or Download voice for available audio files.

Play when my new response is ready applies to the request you just made. Opening Saved responses or loading a session never records, generates or starts a saved rap automatically. Leaving this workspace stops its voice/demo playback and cancels pending auto-play, while a job already submitted to the server may continue in the background. This is the deliberate exception to the mixers’ persistent playback during ordinary workspace navigation.
Customize a voice locally

Open Customize the voice. Pitch shift spans −12 to +12 semitones. Autotune begins at 0% for clean vocals; choose its Key and Scale, then use Melody = Follow the voice for pitch correction or One note, Two notes, Rising, Falling, Arpeggio or Hook for a repeating pitch pattern. Melody octave offers 2–5, and Note length offers half a beat, one beat or two beats. Pitch shift transposes the processed vocal; the instrumental retains its timing and pitch.

items: Select a completed rap under Saved responses. Open Customize the voice and set a modest Pitch shift or Autotune amount.
Press Apply to this rap when enabled. The app uses the retained clean vocal to create another local version without another provider generation request.
Compare the resulting version with the original. Reset effects returns the controls to clean settings for a subsequent application or request.
Generate a new rap if you want a different voice identity or different words. Apply to this rap preserves the source recording’s identity and lyrics.

blocks.text: Recover or cancel work carefully

Do not repeatedly submit a request because generation takes time. Recover response checks the existing request identity after interruption. Cancel stops remaining work but cannot undo a paid call already in flight. Failed voice conversion is reported without substituting another voice. Refresh Saved responses to locate completed work.

blocks.caption: The expanded Voice demos area provides six bundled examples. The screenshot shows stopped demos and an empty response; no provider generation has been run.

title: Saved sessions presets and moving a setup

blocks.text: Sessions is a named setup library opened from the top bar. It captures controls across workspaces together with their referenced completed generated music, rap audio and stems, so you can return to an arrangement or distribute it to several laptops. It is distinct from the academic study’s participant sessions and recorded events. Saving a musical session does not label a new participant, export study data or record a live performance.

blocks.caption: Saved sessions holds named versions of dashboard preferences and their generated audio. Export selected or Export all produces a portable ZIP containing settings and audio.

blocks.text: Save branch and restore a version

items: Prepare the Connections choices, mixer mappings, sound settings and other controls you want to retain. Give signal mixes clear names and wait for selected generated tracks and their stems to finish before saving.

Open Sessions, keep the suggested Version name or enter a descriptive name such as Workshop baseline – browser – slow brightness, then press Save new version. Repeated names receive a numbered suffix.
Make an experiment. Save new version again to preserve both versions. Use Update selected only when you intend to replace the selected version’s settings and audio snapshot.
Choose a version under Saved versions to inspect its details. Rename changes its name; Delete removes that saved settings version.

Press Load to restore the saved audio and controls. The app stops playback and robot/live activity, and does not automatically reconnect live movement or start playback. The normal browser MIDI discovery and permission flow may run after reload.
Check the recording or live address, audio/MIDI output, available tracks and hardware state. Reconnect live data or MIDI where needed, then press Play explicitly.

blocks.text: Sessions retain mixer controls and mappings, shared definitions, prompts and asset IDs, connection preferences, Rap response and robot/drum preferences, and previous-interface settings. The server keeps an immutable copy of referenced completed generated audio, including stems. Running jobs remain separate. Restoration neither repeats a paid request nor verifies a physical instrument’s state.
Export a configuration for six laptops

items: On the source laptop, choose a tested baseline under Saved versions. Press Export selected for one version or Export all for the saved library and its generated audio.
Keep the downloaded ZIP with the workshop setup files. Give the file a version/date in its filename so operators can identify the intended release.
On another laptop, start its own dashboard and open Sessions → Open file…. Select the exported ZIP.

A file with one version loads immediately. For a file with several versions, select one under Saved versions and press Load. Verify the local input/output and separately provide any referenced movement recording that is not bundled with the app.
Use a new local version name for laptop-specific changes, such as its MIDI destination or workshop live-stream address. Export that variant if it needs to be retained outside the browser.

blocks.text: The portable ZIP includes settings, referenced generated audio and completed stems. It excludes movement recordings, microphone input recordings, participant records, the API key, model files and the robot’s head-calibration file. Do not treat it as a complete installation backup. Older Sessions JSON files still open but contain settings and audio references only. Export an older version as ZIP on the original laptop to collect its audio; restore any missing audio there before exporting. Do not indiscriminately clone one laptop’s participant study identity.
Browser storage and recovery

Preferences and named versions belong to this browser profile and page origin; saved audio snapshots live in the server’s session-assets directory. localhost:8790 and 127.0.0.1:8790 are different origins. Clearing site data or changing profiles can make named versions unavailable. Use one address consistently and export important versions as ZIP before moving or clearing either store.

The library supports 50 versions and validates imports. If storage is full or unavailable, keep the page open, export existing versions and check both browser storage and server disk space before retrying. If referenced audio is missing, restore its session ZIP or choose an available track; saving does not silently substitute another track. Open a Sessions ZIP or older Sessions JSON, not an older preset-library file.
Use older presets only in their matching interface

The older Synth interface has mapping tabs and its own Save preset, Open in new tab, Export and Import controls. Its preset library is different from Sessions archives. Previous version in Music mixer likewise retains an older workflow. Use Sessions for a complete new workshop baseline.

title: Observer inspect telemetry and diagnose behavior

blocks.text: Open the read-only Observer from the top bar or http://127.0.0.1:8790/observer/. It helps distinguish a mapping producing values from a later audio/hardware problem. It is not a microphone meter and cannot confirm audible sound or physical robot contact.

blocks.caption: Observer exposes the selected source, transport health, performance state, parameter field and event timeline. Demo data is labeled and must not be mistaken for a connected instrument.

blocks.text: Choose the source intentionally

Source = Auto follows active Signal Lab preview telemetry and falls back to native/demo telemetry when the preview stops. Source = Signal Lab stays locked to the dashboard’s sonification feed. This feed can describe browser-audio playback as well as MIDI commands, so it does not require the Hydrasynth to echo every sent value. In a no-hardware demonstration, the fallback can be labeled Demo data. That display is an interface demonstration, not evidence of a connected synth.

items: Start a simple Synth mixer performance with one mapped parameter.
Open Observer through the top bar so you can return to the workspace without intentionally stopping playback.
Choose Signal Lab if you want to watch only the browser performance. Check the connection label and route before interpreting values.
Search for your mapped parameter. Watch its value and short history while the input changes.
Return to the workspace and press Stop. In Auto, observe the source fallback; in Signal Lab, expect a waiting/inactive state rather than a new performance.

blocks.text: Read the panels

rows: Active voice and route
Shows the known patch/voice and data route. An unknown patch is not proof that patch selection failed; native tracking depends on the messages the synth has transmitted.
Sequence
A counter for observed event ordering. Gaps can indicate missed notifications.
Queue / Jobs / Dropped
Native transport health. Queued events and active jobs should settle after completed work. Rising dropped counts mean the observed history is incomplete.
Tracked held notes
Notes known to the service or feed, plus channel and expression readouts. This is tracked state, not acoustic pitch detection.
Parameter field
Observed or reference parameters, their values, provenance, histories and any takeover windows.
Activity timeline
Recent incoming and scheduled events. Use it to relate a control change to a note, parameter event or job transition.
Snapshot age
How recently a snapshot reached the page. An old snapshot can explain why the display appears frozen.

blocks.text: Filter parameters and understand provenance

Search parameters, CC or NRPN by name or number. The slash shortcut focuses the search box. All shows the available observed view; Changed emphasizes recent changes; User shows front-panel or external MIDI input; Agent shows generated control and automation; Takeover shows currently protected controls. Catalog adds the published reference definitions even when a value has never been observed. A catalog value is reference information, not a live measurement.

Who moved it? distinguishes User, Agent and Agent echo. An echo is an incoming value recognized as matching a recent outgoing command, rather than a new front-panel gesture. The native service normally gives a user-moved CC or NRPN parameter a short takeover window, three seconds by default. Conflicting native automation can be blocked until that window expires. Use this interpretation for native-service telemetry; it is not a claim that every independent Web MIDI sender participates in the same arbitration.
Diagnose a performance in order

items: Confirm the source badge. A lively demo feed does not explain silence from a stopped real transport.
Check snapshot freshness and any connection error. If the page cannot reach the local server, inspect the terminal running the dashboard.
Check whether notes or parameter events appear when expected. If they do not, return to the mixer’s transport, input freshness, mapped destination and enabled state.
If values change but browser sound is silent, check Test sound, mute/solo, faders, filters and Linux output routing.

If MIDI values are sent but the instrument does not respond, check destination, channel, PARAM RX and the instrument’s audio path. For patch tracking, also check its transmitted bank/program settings.

After an unplugged native MIDI device, reconnect it and restart the native dashboard/service as described in the Linux instructions. The native backend reports loss and stops rather than silently switching to another device.

blocks.text: When documenting a fault, record the source mode, route, snapshot age, parameter, error and action taken. A screenshot preserves the visible state; study records provide the fuller history. The bounded on-screen timeline is not a workshop archive.

title: Keirzo hardware connections and first checks

blocks.text: Keirzo setup is the hardware test bench. Open Setup → Keirzo setup, or http://127.0.0.1:8790/#robot-setup. Use it when first connecting a robot, transferring a calibration, testing a part, or investigating a connection fault. Keirzo control is the everyday performance view. Once the rig and saved head range are verified, it can prepare the required hardware when you press Start robot.

Demo mode is not a robot simulator or a motor-output lock. make dashboard-sonify and make dashboard-demo simulate the native Hydrasynth telemetry service, but keep the real robot controls and browser Web MIDI available. A connected robot can move when you press its torque, test, or start controls. Simply opening the dashboard does not connect motors, enable their torque, or start a performance.

blocks.caption: Keirzo setup with the robot disconnected. Connection status and missing devices are expected in this screenshot; the controls operate real hardware when it is connected.

blocks.text: Know which adapter belongs to each part

The head, ribs and arms have three separate USB serial connections. Their identities are saved in config/robot-devices.json using USB vendor ID, product ID and serial number. The current Linux path, such as /dev/ttyUSB0 or /dev/ttyACM0, can change after reconnecting. The saved USB identity lets the dashboard find the same adapter after moving it to another socket or computer.

rows: Head
ROBOTIS OpenRB-150; serial 6430A5355055344E312E3120FF0C0B25
Discovered two-axis head; recorded IDs 0 and 1; 1,000,000 baud
Ribs
FTDI adapter; serial FT78LBUJ
Drumming arms
FTDI adapter; serial FT7WBEBD
LEDs
Pimoroni Plasma 2040 over USB MIDI
Browser MIDI; independent of motor serial connections

blocks.text: The head and drums reuse motor IDs 0 and 1 on different buses. Identify the adapter, not just the motor number. Discovery only reads the computer’s list of serial ports; it does not open a bus or test its motors. A missing or ambiguous USB identity is not replaced with another adapter. Manual selection is available, but a selected port still needs a successful connection check.

items: Connect and power the intended hardware. Close Max, interaction.py and other programs that could own its serial adapters. The legacy interaction.py bridge opens the rib and drum ports and is not needed by these direct dashboard controls.
Open Keirzo setup and use Refresh ports after plugging in or reconnecting an adapter. Confirm the selected adapter for each group against its USB identity.

Use Identify head for the head and Check connection for ribs and arms. These checks use ping/register reads and do not enable torque or move a motor. Inspect every motor reply, position, torque state and reported error.

Resolve missing motors or a mismatched head calibration before using torque or test controls. The tables show timestamped measurements, not continuous position tracking; check again when the physical state may have changed.

blocks.text: Inspect devices from a terminal

.venv/bin/python tools/robot_devices.py
.venv/bin/python -m serial.tools.list_ports -v

These listings help distinguish an absent USB adapter from a motor that does not answer. On Ubuntu, an actual serial permission error may require dialout membership and a logout/login after a group change. Do not run the dashboard as root. If the adapter appears but no motors answer, verify the selected role, power, baud rate and that another serial client is closed. Changing a group’s port requires another check. The dashboard prevents two groups from opening the same adapter.

The Linux port has been tested with virtual MIDI, synthetic audio and simulated serial hardware. The robot and Hydrasynth were not connected for this Linux installation. Earlier physical observations in the repository refer to the recorded rig on macOS; they do not establish that a new laptop, changed mounting, or current sequence has passed a physical acceptance run.

title: Stopping torque and disconnecting

blocks.text: A stop button, torque release and serial disconnect do different things. Torque is the motor’s holding force. A motor can stop receiving new movement commands while remaining powered and holding its position. Conversely, releasing torque can allow an assembly to fall or move under its own weight. Support the head before deliberately releasing its torque.

rows: Top Stop in Keirzo control
Cancels startup or stops robot effects and automatic drumming. Normal LED performance turns off. Stops future rib/head commands; healthy moving drum arms may finish their return.
Does not turn off motor torque or interrupt an already-issued rib/head move. Mixer audio has its own Stop control and is not stopped by this robot control.
Stop in Automatic drumming
Discards upcoming drum hits and lets healthy arms already moving complete their return.
Does not stop LED, rib or head performance. Does not release arm torque. Mixer audio has its own Stop control and is not stopped by this robot control.
Release ribs / Release arms / Release head
Requests torque off for that group. Head release stops head scheduling; arm release cancels pending drum motion/return.
Does not release unrelated motor groups.
Disconnect for a motor group
Closes its serial connection; arm disconnect also cancels the pending return.
Does not turn torque off.
Emergency stop
Cancels live robot patterns, queued motor commands and drum returns, stops head range recording, and requests torque off on already-open, verified buses.
Does not open unknown adapters or guarantee a torque-off write reaches an unavailable motor. Mixer audio has its own Stop control and is not stopped by this robot control.
Reset emergency stop
Clears the software latch.
Does not enable torque, replay cancelled commands or restart drumming.

blocks.text: Use the ordinary stop for planned pauses

Press the top Stop in Keirzo control when ending both robot performances. A head or rib movement already sent to the motor finishes its profile; holding torque stays on. Stop is therefore a controlled sequencing pause rather than an instantaneous mechanical stop. Press Start robot again when ready to prepare the selected effects. Start drumming is separate and must be used when drum hits are wanted.

Changing dashboard workspaces is not a stop: music, connections and robot performance remain active while you navigate. The live browser sequences need the page to stay open. Closing or reloading the page ends browser sequencing, but it is not a reliable substitute for deliberate stopping and releasing the intended groups. Server-run manual strike/return tests can continue across tab changes. A loss of the automatic-drumming heartbeat ends further queued performance after its bounded timeout.
Understand the emergency stop latch

Emergency stop appears in both Keirzo setup and Keirzo control. It is a software stop sent over serial, not a physical power cutoff. The server attempts torque release on connected, verified rib, arm and head buses and reports failed writes. If a motor cannot be reached, the software cannot release it through that connection. Torque off also removes support, so consider the actual head and arm position when operating the rig.

The latch persists across dashboard tabs and page reloads while the server remains running. Correct the cause, read any reported torque-off failures, then use Reset emergency stop. Explicitly prepare/start again after resetting; no cancelled performance resumes by itself. A server restart starts with motor output available but does not open ports or issue motor commands. Restarting the process is not a substitute for a controlled recovery procedure.
Finish a robot session deliberately

items: Use the top Stop and confirm the live performance is stopped. Allow healthy in-progress returns or profile moves to complete when this is an ordinary planned shutdown.

Support the head before using Release head if it should no longer hold its pose. Use Release arms and Release ribs for the groups whose torque should be removed. Read the result of each action; a button click is not proof that every motor received it.
Disconnect the relevant ports once their intended torque state is established. Stop the dashboard with Ctrl+C in its terminal when finished.
Investigate any failed release or lost connection at the actual robot. A serial disconnect or closed browser does not establish the physical state of the rig.

title: Manual rib drum and LED tests

blocks.text: Rib cage

Check connection must read all six rib motors before grouped movement or torque-on becomes available. Press Rib torque on when ready to hold the ribs, set Rib cage position and Duration (ms), then press Test rib cage. Editing a number or slider prepares the requested test; it does not itself send the movement. Expand Individual rib motors to test a single motor with Test position. The Command log records requested commands and results.

The grouped position uses the original Max scale from 0 to 127 and mirrors the two sides. At 0, motors 20–22 target 2450 and motors 25–27 target 1700. At 127, those targets become 4090 and 0 respectively. The default grouped duration is 2500 ms. The test interface accepts 100–5000 ms; this is an interface policy, not a statement of the motor’s mechanical limits.

Before a direct move, the service rechecks the motors and requires torque on, position operating mode and time-based profiles. It does not change those modes for you. It writes the profile duration and goal position and checks the replies. A successful register acknowledgement confirms receipt of the command, not physical arrival. Release ribs affects only these six motors and remains available while emergency stop is latched. On a verified rib bus it attempts each release even when a motor fails to reply.
Drumming arms

items: Select the separate drum adapter and press Check connection. Confirm all four motor replies, torque states and errors.

Press Arm torque on + rest. This enables holding torque and returns all four arms to configured rest over two seconds, including arms that were already powered or outside their normal playing ranges. Wait for the confirmed ready/rest result.

Press Test strike for one part. The test first raises that arm to rest over 500 ms, checks that it is within 20 ticks of rest, sends the configured hit, and returns it to the same raised rest with a 150 ms profile.

Wait for the complete result before another test. Only one manual strike runs at a time; clicking again does not queue another hit. If an arm is outside its playing range, use Arm torque on + rest before striking.

rows: Kick / 0
150 ms
Ride / 1
150 ms
Snare / 2
150 ms
Hi-hat / 3
200 ms

blocks.text: These are raw Dynamixel ticks from the repository’s Max bounds and stroke profiles, not degrees. Ride and Snare were physically exchanged: motor 1 is Ride, motor 2 is Snare, while their motor-specific positions remain attached to those IDs. The hi-hat uses the in-range second source profile rather than expanding its bound to include an old out-of-range profile. Advanced manual position controls send a single move without an automatic return; choose them deliberately.

Release arms affects IDs 0–3 on the selected drum bus, removes holding torque and cancels a pending return. Disconnect also cancels the return but leaves torque unchanged. The controller checks rest arrival rather than treating elapsed profile time as proof of position. The automatic performance engine additionally insets boundary rest goals for settling tolerance, including hi-hat rest at 2590.
LED controller

Connect the Pimoroni Plasma 2040 over USB and allow MIDI access in the browser. Keirzo setup finds a Plasma 2040/Pimoroni output automatically; it does not fall back to the synth. It normally appears as Plasma 2040 CircuitPython usb_midi.ports[0]. A new browser needs its own MIDI permission. Use Retry MIDI connection after granting permission if access was denied.

Choose a non-black Colour and Brightness above 0%, then press Test colour. Press LEDs off to send black. Connecting MIDI or changing the colour picker alone does not send a test. If discovery succeeds but the strip stays dark, check the hint beside the controller and the board’s LED program: a MIDI device in the list proves USB discovery, not that its LED firmware is running. The current automatic matching assumes one matching LED board.

The checked-in lights/code.py fills 96 LEDs using a two-message RGB command on MIDI channel 1: Note On with note 1 and red as velocity, followed by Polyphonic Key Pressure with green as note and blue as pressure. Components are 0–127 and scaled by the firmware. LED control is independent of motor torque and the serial connections. Reconnecting the board does not automatically change its colour.

title: Head calibration and preparation

blocks.text: Powered head movement requires a saved range for the same physical head assembly and a matching connection. Copy var/robot/head-calibration.json from the computer previously used with that same mounted robot, or record the intended travel manually. The file lives under Git-ignored var/, so cloning the repository does not bring it to a new laptop. A saved browser session is not a replacement for this file.

blocks.caption: The Head identification and Record head range controls. With hardware disconnected, the manual shows their location rather than fabricated motor readings.

blocks.text: Identify before recording

The documented rig uses a two-axis 2XL430-W250-T, model 1090, on its own OpenRB-150 bus at 1,000,000 baud. Recorded IDs are 0 and 1, but discovery reads the responding IDs and model rather than assuming factory IDs. The model’s factory baud is 57,600, which matters only for a different unconfigured setup. Select the actual adapter and configured baud, then press Identify head. Review the two measured positions, torque, modes and errors.

With the head upright, Record upright position saves a read-only reference in server memory. It does not centre the head, enable torque or establish travel limits. The reference is lost on server restart or a change of adapter, baud or identified axes. Motor factory limits of 0–4095 are not safe mounted-head limits. Do not use historical positions as a generic calibration for another assembly.
Record travel with torque off

items: Support the head. If torque is enabled, use Release head and confirm torque off before moving it by hand. Both axes must respond with torque off before recording starts.
Place the head upright and press Start recording. The centre is taken from an upright reference for this connection when available; otherwise it uses the starting positions.
Move each axis gently through the travel intended for use, stopping before resistance. Watch the Current, Minimum and Maximum readings and name the axes as you identify them.
Press Stop recording. If needed, return the head to the desired centre and press Capture centre to read both motors again.
Review both axes, then press Save range. Each needs a nonzero span and a centre inside that span. The previous saved range is replaced only after validation and a successful file write.
Keep a backup of the calibration with this same mounted head. On another laptop, confirm that the loaded range reports a matching connection after identification.

blocks.text: Recording runs on the server and continues across workspace changes. A read error, torque becoming enabled, connection change or emergency stop stops it; captured samples remain available, but unsaved recording state disappears when the server restarts. Saving a range neither enables torque nor starts performance. Recorded positions describe observed individual travel, not proof that every simultaneous two-axis pose is mechanically safe.
Prepare the head for powered movement

A head with torque off can rest below its saved range. Support it, release torque if necessary, and gently hold both axes near their saved centre and inside their saved ranges. Identify head reads the current pose without moving it. In Keirzo control, enable the Head, choose Manual Busy-ness 0 for an initial modest activity setting, and press Start robot. Preparation checks the saved identity and current pose, preloads that measured pose and enables holding torque. It does not command a centring move. Keep supporting the head until holding torque is confirmed, clear of the moving joints; the selected head performance follows preparation.

Powered commands require the saved adapter identity, baud, two motor IDs and model to match. They also require healthy readbacks, position mode 3, time profiles and an in-range measured pose. They are blocked during range recording, for secondary-ID aliases, or when automatic torque-on by goal update is enabled. The application does not change EEPROM settings or factory position limits to bypass these checks. Older calibrations tied only to a port path may not follow an adapter to a new port.

For historical reference only, the recorded assembly had centres 2075 and 2529, with ranges 1408–2654 and 1948–3071 for IDs 0 and 1. Always use the current verified range displayed in Setup. The documented rig has also shown small-movement vibration whose physical cause remains unresolved. The current profiles avoid very slow motion; position gains were not changed. Its wider flowing sequence still needs a physical check on the actual assembly.

For diagnosis, GET /api/robot/head/diagnostics samples an already-open identified head without connecting it or moving it. It reports measured position, internal trajectory, goal, output, inferred load and supply voltage. Ordinary status tables use cached readings. Keep the exact diagnostic and visible physical behavior together when reporting a problem; a requested target alone does not show that the head arrived.

title: Keirzo control coordinated lights ribs and head

blocks.text: Open Use → Keirzo control or http://127.0.0.1:8790/#robot-control. Choose Follow → Music mixer or Synth mixer. The BPM and beat indicators show the chosen player’s clock; there is no independent robot tempo. The link next to Follow opens that mixer. The selection also applies to Automatic drumming, so changing it changes the source for lights, ribs, beat-synced head motion and drums together.

blocks.caption: Keirzo control groups the performance transport, source following, LED palette, rib breathing and head activity. Start robot prepares real motor hardware.

blocks.text: Prepare and start

items: Choose the Follow source and configure the effects you intend to use. Prepare a saved matching head range and support the head near its centre if Head Enabled is selected.

Press Start robot. Read the preparation status while it finds connections and enables required torque. It always prepares all four drumming arms at raised rest, even if LEDs are the only selected effect or all effects are disabled.

Wait for preparation to finish before expecting performance. Missing arms, an active strike/drumming sequence, motor mode errors or a mismatched head range can prevent startup. Stop drumming before trying rest preparation again.
Start playback in the chosen mixer for synced effects. Press Start drumming separately if actual drum hits are desired.
Use the top Stop to stop both robot effects and automatic drumming. Navigate between workspaces freely during a performance; the dashboard page must remain open.

blocks.text: The synchronisation comes from the dashboard’s playback clock, not microphone beat detection. When playback stops, synced effects wait. Changing Follow cancels queued drum hits; explicitly press Start drumming again for the new source. A saved session restores preferences passively and does not start robot playback.
LED performance

Enable the LEDs, choose Aurora, Firelight, Ocean or Candy, or edit the four palette colours. Solid colour uses the first colour. Palette cycle advances through the palette, and Beat pulse varies brightness on the beat. Change colour every selects ¼, ½, 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 beats. Brightness scales the overall output. Start robot finds the same automatically detected Pimoroni controller used in Setup. It also prepares the arms even for an LED-only performance.
Rib breathing

Enable Rib breathing, set Minimum position and Maximum position on the 0–127 scale, and choose how many beats pass before moving to the next position. Four beats means four beats outward and four back: an eight-beat full cycle. The motion uses the same mirrored mapping and bounds as Setup.
